claims.text: Machine-learning-based optimization of process conditions can overcome residual thermal stresses in additively manufactured AlCrFeNiSi miniature components.
Machine-learning-based optimization of process conditions can overcome degraded mechanical properties in additively manufactured AlCrFeNiSi miniature components.
Machine-learning-based optimization can reduce the processing complexity of additively manufactured AlCrFeNiSi miniature components.
Laser power, scan speed, and powder composition are proposed optimization variables.
The proposed intervention is applicable to laser powder bed fusion of AlCrFeNiSi miniature components.
Microstructural evolution and defect formation mediate the effects of optimized processing conditions.
Optimized process conditions reduce residual thermal stresses.
Optimized process conditions improve mechanical properties.
Optimized process conditions increase processing efficiency.
Relative to conventional high-thermal-load additive manufacturing, the optimized components will have improved tensile strength or hardness.
Relative to conventional high-thermal-load additive manufacturing, the optimized components will have lower residual thermal stresses.
Relative to conventional high-thermal-load additive manufacturing, the optimized process will have greater processing efficiency.
